items.title: sync-api: migration 5 and a change number on every transcription write
items.red_not_run: the schema, the store change and their tests land together: on the base the new tests do not compile (the store and the columns are absent), so there is no assertion-red leg; the mutants carry the proof

edits.anchor: "ALTER TABLE accounts ADD COLUMN change_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (change_seq >= 0)"
edits.replacement: "ALTER TABLE accounts ADD COLUMN change_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (change_seq >= -1)"

expected_red: the new columns refuse a negative counter, a negative purge mark and a delete flag of 2

edits.anchor: "ALTER TABLE accounts ADD COLUMN purged_through INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (purged_through >= 0)"
edits.replacement: "ALTER TABLE accounts ADD COLUMN purged_through INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (purged_through >= -1)"

expected_red: the new columns refuse a negative counter, a negative purge mark and a delete flag of 2
entries.rule: the purge mark check lets -1 through

edits.anchor: "ALTER TABLE transcriptions ADD COLUMN deleted INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (deleted IN (0, 1))"
edits.replacement: "ALTER TABLE transcriptions ADD COLUMN deleted INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (deleted IN (0, 1, 2))"

expected_red: the new columns refuse a negative counter, a negative purge mark and a delete flag of 2

edits.anchor: "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX transcriptions_account_change_no ON transcriptions (account_id, change_no)"

expected_red: a fresh database ends at the latest version with the change columns, the delete flag, the pulled change column and the unique index
the unique index refuses a repeated change number of one account and accepts it on another account
entries.rule: the index is not unique: two rows of one account can share a number

edits.anchor: "SELECT id, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY id) AS n " +
edits.replacement: "SELECT id, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY id DESC) AS n " +

expected_red: an upgrade from version 4 keeps every row, numbers each account from 1 in id order and sets each counter
entries.rule: the backfill numbers rows from the newest: the id order is reversed

edits.anchor: "SELECT id, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY id) AS n " +
edits.replacement: "SELECT id, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY id) AS n " +

expected_red: an upgrade from version 4 keeps every row, numbers each account from 1 in id order and sets each counter
entries.rule: the backfill numbers all rows together instead of per account

edits.anchor: "UPDATE accounts SET change_seq = (SELECT count(*) FROM transcriptions WHERE account_id = accounts.id)"
edits.replacement: "UPDATE accounts SET change_seq = (SELECT count(*) + 1 FROM transcriptions WHERE account_id = accounts.id)"

expected_red: an upgrade from version 4 keeps every row, numbers each account from 1 in id order and sets each counter
entries.rule: the starting counter is one too high

edits.anchor: "ALTER TABLE tokens ADD COLUMN last_pulled_change INTEGER"
edits.replacement: "ALTER TABLE tokens ADD COLUMN last_pulled_change INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0"

expected_red: an upgrade from version 4 keeps every row, numbers each account from 1 in id order and sets each counter
entries.rule: a token starts with a pulled number of 0 instead of never pulled

expected_red: a fresh database ends at the latest version with the change columns, the delete flag, the pulled change column and the unique index

edits.anchor: const val BUMP_CHANGE_SEQ_SQL = "UPDATE accounts SET change_seq = change_seq + 1 WHERE id = ?"
edits.replacement: const val BUMP_CHANGE_SEQ_SQL = "UPDATE accounts SET change_seq = change_seq + 2 WHERE id = ?"

expected_red: new client ids take 1 2 3 on one account while another account starts at 1
a replace takes the next number and bumps change_seq
entries.rule: the counter moves by two: numbers skip

edits.anchor:
val changeNo = bumpChangeSeq(connection, accountId)
                    replaceRow(connection, accountId, clientId, keyVersion, encrypted, nowMs, changeNo)
edits.replacement:
val changeNo = 0L
                    replaceRow(connection, accountId, clientId, keyVersion, encrypted, nowMs, changeNo)

expected_red: a replace takes the next number and bumps change_seq
entries.rule: a replace takes no new number

expected_red: a deleted stored row at a lower version answers NoOp to a higher push with no number taken
entries.rule: the deleted rule is gone: a higher push replaces a deleted row

expected_red: new client ids take 1 2 3 on one account while another account starts at 1
entries.rule: an insert writes number 0 instead of the taken number
equivalent for the tests: a missing account is refused earlier, when the store reads the account's key version, so the bump never sees zero rows
